description: We are a team of Computer Science and Engineering students focused on developing innovative space-tech solutions. For NASA’s CLPS Lunar Moon challenge, we aim to create an interactive platform that visualizes lunar landing sites, mission data, and surface information. We combine coding, data analysis, UI/UX, and research skills to make complex lunar data easy to explore and understand.
summary: CORE LOGICS transforms scattered lunar information into a single mission-planning workflow. Our platform combines mission exploration, landing-site analysis, terrain and environmental conditions, interactive lunar visualization and route planning. Users can move from exploring a lunar mission to selecting a site, analyzing its conditions, configuring waypoints and reviewing route feasibility. The project is designed to make early-stage lunar mission analysis faster, more understandable and more data-driven.
details:
CORE LOGICS – CLPS Mission Explorer is an integrated lunar mission analysis and landing-site decision-support platform designed to make lunar exploration data easier to explore, compare, and use for early-stage mission planning.

The project addresses the challenge that important lunar mission and landing-site information is distributed across different sources and tools. Selecting a suitable lunar site may require considering terrain, elevation, slope, illumination, temperature, water-ice indicators, radiation, and Earth-communication conditions. CORE LOGICS brings these concepts together into a single interactive workflow so users can move from mission exploration to site analysis and mission planning.

The platform provides an interactive Mission Explorer, 2D and 3D lunar visualization, landing-site condition analysis, and a Mission Planner. Users can explore missions and lunar locations, examine site conditions, select a starting location and destination, add intermediate waypoints, and review route-related information such as distance, elevation, slope changes, estimated duration, and terrain-based risk considerations. The planning workflow demonstrated by our prototype includes Shackleton Rim as the start location and de Gerlache Rim as the destination, with two intermediate waypoints and objectives related to scientific payloads and terrain analysis.

The technical foundation of the prototype includes React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js for interactive 3D visualization, 2D polar/global maps, NASA-referenced data services, NASA Images API, SPICE-based Sun/Earth geometry, local caching, and archive fallback. The architecture follows a Live Data → Cache → Archive Fallback approach to improve resilience and provide transparent information about data sources.

The main benefit of CORE LOGICS is reducing the need to switch between multiple tools during early-stage lunar mission analysis. It provides a more organized and understandable workflow for exploring lunar missions, comparing site conditions, and configuring mission scenarios.

The intended impact is to support mission planners, payload teams, students, researchers, and future lunar exploration or rover studies. The platform can help users understand complex lunar information through interactive visualization and structured mission planning.

The creativity of the project comes from combining lunar mission exploration, landing-site decision support, environmental and terrain considerations, interactive 2D/3D visualization, and mission planning into one platform. Instead of functioning only as a lunar map, CORE LOGICS connects data exploration with an actionable mission-planning workflow.

During development, our team considered usability, clarity of visualization, data-source transparency, scalability, resilience to unavailable data, and the need to present complex lunar information in a simple and understandable way. The current prototype provides a foundation that can be expanded with AI-based landing-site recommendations, higher-resolution terrain and hazard layers, advanced rover route optimization, and expanded illumination and communication analysis.
